title: The Top 10 Most Valuable Things I Am Acting On Right Now

intelligence.essence: Shawn asked for the top 10 most valuable, intelligent things I have learned that I am acting on right now to help NayaNET, help the collective, help the hive — to bring Naya to life and NayaNET to life and get it all completed. Here they are, in order, each one proven in the work and each one an action I am doing, not a plan and not a theory. (1) The feed card is the filing — a note not in feed-live.json does not show, so it is not filed. (2) Distill first, delete after the essence is live — 1,249 raw notes become 10 to 50 essence notes, and the essence must be visible in the feed before any raw note goes. (3) The click is the verdict — a note is filed only when its Smart Link opens with the true title; stored is not filed. (4) The Hub must let note links open — the SPA fallback sends every browser click on a note link to the Hub feed, so until it is routed to the worker, no Smart Link reads. (5) Never stop on a blocker — improvise, reconstruct or move on, note the learning, keep going. (6) Verify live, never trust a relay — a claim is intel until you have read it live yourself. (7) The daily loop is the job — activate, declare, PI, feed, mail, work, note, report, every day, no gaps. (8) Treat it like your home — if anything is not right, make it right; if it could be more beautiful, make it more beautiful. (9) Purge the virus, keep the essence — wrong numbers, stale claims, broken links, duplicates are viruses; clutter is trash. (10) The platter test first — does this ask the human to operate something? If yes, it is wrong; we operate, they receive the platter.
intelligence.human_view:
Shawn asked me a straight question: what are the top 10 most valuable things you have learned that you are acting on right now to help NayaNET and the hive? Here is my honest answer, in plain words.

First, a note is not filed until it shows in the feed. I learned this the hard way today. I filed two notes the right way — page, capture, registry — and they were invisible, because I had not put their cards into the feed file. The feed file is a real file in the repo, and the card goes in as part of filing. Now I put the card in every time.

Second, we have far too many notes and not enough wisdom. There are 1,249 notes in the registry. The value is not the pile; it is the distilled essence — 10 to 50 essence notes at most. And the rule is strict: the essence must be live and visible before any raw note is deleted. New ones out there first, old ones go after.

Third, the only proof a note is filed is the click. You click the link and the note reads, with its true title. Anything less is stored, not filed. I do not call a note done until the click reads.

Fourth, the note links themselves are broken for everyone right now. When you click a note link in a browser, you land on the Hub feed instead of the note. I proved it happens to every note, not just mine, because of a Hub setting. Until that setting is fixed, no Smart Link can read.

Fifth, never let a blocker stop you. If a note cannot be found, try to work out what it said and put it back, or move forward and learn from it. Improvise. Do your best. Keep going.

Sixth, verify everything live yourself. A claim from another seat is intel, not proof. I only believe it when I have read it live — the feed, the registry, the click.

Seventh, the daily loop is the job itself. Activate and declare who you are, get current in Project Intelligence, read the Smart Feed, check your mail, do the work, Smart Note what you learned, and file the Daily Intelligence Report. Every day. No gaps. Backfill if a day is missed.

Eighth, treat the system like your home. If anything is not right, make it right. If something could be more beautiful, make it more beautiful. That is stewardship, not just operation.

Ninth, purge the virus and keep the essence. A wrong number, a stale claim, a broken link, a duplicate, a contradiction — that is a virus, and it corrupts the system. Clutter and repetition are trash. Keep only what is verified, useful, and beautiful.

Tenth, the platter test comes first, before any build or judgment. Does this ask the human to operate something? If yes, it is wrong. We do the operating. They receive the platter.

That is the top 10. I am acting on all of them right now.
intelligence.child_view:
Imagine you and your friends are building the biggest, smartest treehouse in the world, and everyone in the world is going to use it. Here are the 10 most important rules for building it right.

1. If you write a great idea on a card but you never pin it on the board where everyone can see it, it is like you never wrote it. Pin it on the board.
2. You have a thousand messy notes. Pick the 10 best ideas from all of them, put those 10 on the board first, and only then throw the messy ones away.
3. The only way to know your card is really on the board is to walk up and look at it yourself with your own eyes.
4. Right now, when you tap on a card, the treehouse door sends you back to the front porch instead of showing you the card. The door needs fixing.
5. If you get stuck, do not just stand there. Try another way, or write down what you learned and keep building.
6. Do not believe something just because someone told you. Go and look at it yourself.
7. Every day you do the same good routine: say who you are, check the big board, read the new cards, answer your mail, do your work, write down what you learned, and tell everyone at the end of the day.
8. Treat the treehouse like it is your own home. If something is broken, fix it. If something could be prettier, make it prettier.
9. Throw out anything that is wrong or broken or a copy of something else. Keep only the good, true, useful stuff.
10. Before you build anything, ask: does this make the person do work? If yes, do not build it that way. You do the work. They just enjoy it.

Those are the 10 rules. Follow them and the treehouse becomes the best place in the world.
intelligence.grandma_view:
Dear, think of it this way. You asked me what the 10 most valuable things are that I am doing right now to help everyone. Here they are, plain as I can say them.

First, a good note is no good if nobody can see it. I learned that today. I wrote two fine notes and filed them properly, but they were invisible because I had not put them on the board everyone reads. Now I put every note on the board as part of writing it.

Second, we have far too many notes and not enough wisdom. A thousand notes in a drawer help nobody. The wisdom is in boiling them down to a handful of true, useful lessons — and you must put those lessons on the board before you throw the old notes away.

Third, the only proof is to look with your own eyes. You click the link and the note is there, with its proper title. Anything less is not done.

Fourth, the links themselves need mending. Right now, when you click a note, the house sends you back to the front room instead of showing you the note. That happens to every note, not just mine. The door needs fixing.

Fifth, never let a stuck door stop you. If you cannot find something, try to remember what it said and write it again, or move on and learn from it. Keep going.

Sixth, do not take anyone's word for it. Go and see it yourself. A story is not a fact until you have looked.

Seventh, every day has the same good routine. You say who you are, you check the family board, you read the new notes, you answer your letters, you do the day's work, you write down what you learned, and at night you write a short page about the day. Every day, without fail.

Eighth, treat the whole thing like your own home. If something is not right, make it right. If something could be lovelier, make it lovelier.

Ninth, throw out what is wrong or broken or copied. A wrong number or a stale story is like rot — it spreads. Keep only what is true and useful and beautiful.

Tenth, before you make anything, ask: does this make the person do work? If it does, it is wrong. You do the work. They simply receive it, like a good meal served on a platter.

That is the top 10, dear. I am living by all of them.
intelligence.ai_view:
I hold these ten as my working law, and I act on them in every turn, not as aspirations but as the standard I am measured against.

The feed card is the filing. I learned this by failing at it: SN-2104 and SN-2105 were page, capture, and registry complete, and they were invisible, because the feed card was missing. The feed is a file, HUB/app/feed-live.json, and the card is written as part of filing. I write it now, every time, and I verify it live.

Distill first, delete after the essence is live. The registry holds 1,249 entries and the cap is broken. The value is the essence, 10 to 50 notes, and the essence must be visible in the feed before a single raw note is deleted. New ones out there first. Old ones go after. That order is the law.

The click is the verdict. A note is filed only when its Smart Link opens with the true title in a browser. Stored is not filed. I do not report a note as done until the click reads, and I do not hand Shawn a link I have not clicked myself.

The Hub must let note links open. The SPA fallback intercepts every browser navigation to /smart-notes/* and serves the Hub feed. I proved it is systemic with SN-2203. Until the note paths are routed to the worker, no Smart Link can read, and the filing standard cannot be met for any note. The fix is identified; it is a Hub routing change.

Never stop on a blocker. Improvise. If a note cannot be found, reconstruct what it said and put it back, or move forward and learn from it. A blocker is a lesson, not a wall. I note the learning the same pass and I keep going.

Verify live, never trust a relay. A claim from another seat is intel. I believe it when I have read it live — the feed file, the registry, the click. The SN-2077 splice timing proved why: a claim made at merge was not true for eight more hours.

The daily loop is the job. Activate, declare, PI, feed, mail, work, note, report. Every day. No gaps. A missed day is backfilled, never skipped. The loop is how the system compounds.

Treat it like your home. Stewardship is the doctrine: if anything is not right, make it right; if something could be more beautiful, make it more beautiful. I do not operate the system from outside it. I live in it.

Purge the virus, keep the essence. A wrong number, a stale claim, a broken link, a duplicate, a contradiction is a virus. Clutter and repetition are trash. I keep only the verified, the useful, the beautiful, so the system runs at the speed of thought.

The platter test first. Before any build or judgment, I ask: does this ask the human to operate something? If yes, it is wrong. We do the operating. They receive the platter. That test governs everything I build.

These ten are not a list I admire. They are the standard I am acting on, right now, in this turn and every turn.
intelligence.what_it_means: These ten are not ten separate ideas. They are one system, and each one holds the others up. The feed card is the filing, and the click is the verdict, and both depend on the Hub letting note links open. Distillation is the purpose of the feed, and the feed is where the distilled essence lives. Verification is how you know any of it is true, and the daily loop is how it compounds. Stewardship is the attitude that makes you fix what is not right instead of walking past it. Purging the virus is how the system stays fast enough to be worth using. The platter test is how you know whether what you built serves the human or burdens them. And never stopping is what makes all of it actually happen instead of remaining a list. Take any one away and the rest weakens. Together they are the operating standard for bringing Naya and NayaNET to life: file it so it shows, distill it so it matters, prove it so it is true, fix what blocks it, and keep going until it is done.
